column1: # ---- Frame rate ----
# The Switch version runs at 30 fps: the frame ratio main+0x6e6cc4 computes is base / the fps the game's controller picked (60 / 30 = 2 at every frame). patches.py FRAME_STEP (v131072 main)
# swaps in the host's step, so the host presents at 60 fps, 30 when 60 does not hold, and game time = real time at either rate. 0 = the Switch original
# Off until it is checked on the phone (2026-11-13): with the cap at 60 and a pack whose main was rewritten before patches.py had the stub, the game would run at twice
# real time. The stub is in patches.py and does nothing at target 0 (the state page holds 0: every frame takes the game's own fdiv)
# fps_target
# 30 (2026-11-15, the plan of that day, P1): the Switch's own rate, with the frame step's ratio at the host's 2 vsyncs, so game time is real time. At 0 the ratio stays 2
# whatever the frame took: the POCO F7 Ultra's Kokiri Forest without frame generation runs 28-33 ms frames (30-36 fps), so the game ran up to 1.17 times real time, and its
# frames showed 25 and 33 ms in turn. With 30: 30.0 fps in all six runs (dm/tools/android_bench.py), every frame 33.3 ms on screen at p50 and p95, 78-80 % of frames
# within 2 ms of 33.3 (docs/RESULTADOS-ETAPA1-2026-11-15.md). 60 with fps_hold went to a 3-vsync hold (22.9 fps) in one of two runs: the frame costs about 2.1 vsyncs there
fps_target
# fps_hold off (2026-11-16): at the 30 cap the hold stays at 2 vsyncs, a frame that runs long shows for 3 and the time it lost is paid back with steps of 3, so game time
# stays real time. With on, three late frames (loading's, at every start) stepped the hold to 3 for good: the GPU clock falls at the longer hold, so the cost never looked
# like 2 vsyncs again. POCO F7 Ultra (891.14), Link's porch, two runs each (dm/tools/android_bench.py): mesh geometry off, on 20.0 / 20.0 fps, off 30.0 / 30.0 fps
# (frames 33.3 ms at p50, 35.5-35.7 at p95, game time 1.004 of real time); mesh geometry on, on 19.9 / 17.9 fps, off 22.2 / 20.9 fps at 1.002-1.003 of real time (frames
# shown 33 and 50 ms in turn where on held a steady 50). (On 2026-11-12, before the payback, off ran the door's 25 fps at about 0.83 of real time.) The launcher passes this
# row as DM_FPS_HOLD (Profile.fpsHold), so packs prepared before it take it too
fps_hold
